Unauthenticated MQTT Access [Spoofing, Information Disclosure, CWE-306] on IoT Devices, MQTT Protocol, IoT Core: Without proper authentication, attackers can connect to the MQTT broker and publish malicious data or subscribe to sensitive data streams. An attacker could spoof an IoT device and inject false sensor readings, potentially causing incorrect energy management decisions or data pollution.

Missing Network Security Controls [Information Disclosure, Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on All AWS Services, Data Flow Paths: Services are not properly isolated in VPCs with appropriate security groups and NACLs, allowing potential lateral movement and unauthorized access. An attacker who gains access to one component could potentially access other services due to lack of network segmentation.

Lack of Transport Layer Security [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-319] on All Data Transfer Paths, API Endpoints, Service Communications: Data transmitted between services without TLS encryption is vulnerable to interception and manipulation. An attacker performing man-in-the-middle attacks could intercept and potentially modify data being transmitted between services.

Insufficient PII Protection in ML Pipeline [Information Disclosure, CWE-359] on S3 Processed Data, SageMaker, Glue ETL: ML models trained on datasets containing PII could potentially memorize and leak this information through model outputs or parameters. An attacker could query the ML model in specific ways to extract PII that was inadvertently included in the training data.

Inadequate Data Lake Access Controls [Information Disclosure, Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-264] on S3 Buckets, Glue Catalog, Lake Formation, Athena, QuickSight: Without proper RBAC, users might have excessive permissions to data lake resources, violating the principle of least privilege. A user with overly broad permissions could access or modify data they shouldn't have access to, or grant permissions to other users.

Insecure Data Storage Configuration [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-732] on S3 Raw Data, S3 Processed Data, Timestream, Redshift: Misconfigured storage services could allow unauthorized access or modification of data through various attack vectors. An attacker could exploit misconfigured bucket policies or encryption settings to access or modify sensitive data.

Insufficient Monitoring and Incident Detection [Repudiation, CWE-778] on All Services: Without proper monitoring and logging, security incidents may not be detected or may be detected too late to prevent damage. An attacker could perform malicious activities without detection due to insufficient monitoring.
